title: Degree-zero naturality square for canonical base change without flatness
statement: Choose shared derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Let f:X→S, g:S′→S, g′:X′→X and f′:X′→S′ be scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme] with g′≫f=f′≫g. Assume injective resolutions in X′.Modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For any O_X-module M, let E=M[0], H=H^0 on S′, c:g′*f*≅f′*g* be the ordinary composition comparison [def-pc-module-pullback], and m the ordinary mate of c.inv followed by g′* of the counit [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Let p_a(N):La*(N[0])→(a*N)[0] be canonicalSinglePullbackMap [lem-pc-canonical-single-pullback-comparison], u_f(M):(f_*M)[0]→Rf_*(M[0]) be canonicalSingleDirectImageMap [lem-pc-canonical-single-direct-image-comparison], k:H((g*f_*M)[0])≅g*f_*M the single-complex homology identification, and z:H(Rf′_*((g′*M)[0]))≅f′_*g′*M the unbounded-to-classical right-derived degree-zero comparison followed by rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf. Then H(p_g(f_*M))≫k.hom≫m = H(Lg*(u_f(M)))≫H(beta_E)≫H(Rf′_*(p_g′(M)))≫z.hom, where beta is the canonical derived base-change map [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. There is no flatness, invertibility, higher-vanishing or cartesian hypothesis.

proof.text: Use the single-module adjunction transpose for f at its ordinary counit. Invert the Hom equivalence to obtain Lf*(u_f(M)) followed by the derived counit = p_f(f_*M) followed by the single ordinary counit.

Use naturality of the derived composition comparison along u_f(M) and the pullback-square identity with a the ordinary counit. Apply the pinned f-prime derived Hom equivalence, using its naturality in both variables and the single-module transpose for f-prime. This proves canonicalSingleMateSquare in the derived category.

Apply H-zero to canonicalSingleMateSquare. Naturality of singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso moves the ordinary mate past the single homology identification. Replace the target single identification by H-zero of the direct-image unit followed by its fixed comparison, using canonicalDirectImageH0Unit. Reassociate and use preservation of composition to conclude.

theorem canonicalDegreeZeroMateSquare
    {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S')
    (h : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g)
    [HasInjectiveResolutions X'.Modules] (M : X.Modules) :
    let E := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj M
    let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S'.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let c := (pullbackComp g' f).app ((pushforward f).obj M) ≪≫
      (pullbackCongr h).app ((pushforward f).obj M) ≪≫
      ((pullbackComp f' g).app ((pushforward f).obj M)).symm
    let k := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S'.toRingedSpace)) 0).app
        ((pullback g).obj ((pushforward f).obj M))
    H.map (canonicalSinglePullbackMap g ((pushforward f).obj M)) ≫ k.hom ≫
        (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').homEquiv _ _
          (c.inv ≫ (pullback g').map ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M)) =
      H.map ((derivedPullback g).map (canonicalSingleDirectImageMap f M)) ≫
        H.map (schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f f' g g' h E) ≫
        H.map ((schemeDerivedDirectImage f').map (canonicalSinglePullbackMap g' M)) ≫
        (canonicalDirectImageH0Iso f' ((pullback g').obj M)).hom
